What a find!
Feb 2018 • Couples
Thap Nga -Binh Xuyen 2 is a restaurant that is off the beaten path. Locals who know good food make up the majority of patrons.

After parking outside the restaurant there are a number of sculptures which provide good picture taking opportunities.

Upon entering I was overwhelmed by the size. We walked quite a distance before we arrived at our table which was right on the river. Watching it grow dark was a pleasant experience. There were no insects to bother us.

As I said the restaurant is huge. It easily could accommodate hundreds of diners but our table was in a quiet location on a Friday evening. 

The menu is extensive. Only one copy was provided to my Vietnamese companion. i requested my own copy and quickly saw that it is entirely written in Vietnamese. However there are many pictures.

The restaurant is so large that the servers use bicycles and roller skates to travel up and back the wide aisles. 

Portions are enormous. Snails, which I don't eat, were plentiful and plumb. i was told they were delicious. I ordered a chicken dish which was ample enough for 3 or 4 people to share. The chicken came whole and was cut up by our server at an adjacent serving station. An excellent choice.

Local beer was a fine and inexpensive accompanyment to our meal. We enjoyed Saigon Gold which is a limited edition brew that i had never seen before.

Service was friendly and efficient. There are enough young servers so that you will be able to find someone who can speak English.

A family fisherman's paradise
Mar 2017 • Family
We were looking for an ordinary outing and stumbelled on this extraordinary restaurant. If you live to go fishing and are looking to go out for dinner with the family, this is the place for you. 

The setting is lavish and extensive. It looks like it is designed to accommodate large business groups and weddings, but a section is devoted to smaller tables. They had no problem accommodating our group of 12. In fact they did really well with our mostly 6-12 aged children, while the dads went fishing.

There was something for everyone and the serving sizes are large. They were kind enough to down scale our order, knowing it was going to be too much food. The price was reasonable considering the quality of the setting and service. The waiters actually wore roller skates to speed up service over this extensive restaurant.

The fishing was really inexpensive at 10k a rod, and it came with bait.

The foyer aquarium showed an extensive selection of fish, but they came at a premium price.

A great outing for the family and a great venue fir large groups.

You Won't Believe This Place... Absolutely Fantastic!!!
Mar 2016 • Couples
Wow! My wife and I are seasoned world travelers, but have never experienced a dinner quite like this. Thap Nga was recommended by a British friend who recently lived in Ho Chi Minh City with his Vietnamese wife. Since nobody at the Renaissance Hotel knew of this restaurant, and since it was about a 30-minute taxi ride from our riverside hotel, I suspect this is not a hot tourist spot. This was confirmed by our first dining experience that evening as the only non-locals we saw.

This is not just a restaurant. Thap Nga is truly an event. I'm told it seats 500 guests in its massive, outdoor but well covered dining areas surrounded by ponds & waterways -- almost a theme park atmosphere. The facilities are new, clean, and beautifully laid out with many sights and appointments nicely lit. We went for dinner at sunset and would recommend this time, as the setting is quite lovely. 

We know Vietnamese cuisine quite well, but were awed by the multi-page menu booklet. No English, but photos on about half of the selections, which makes choosing items fairly easy with some study. However, our pointing and quizzical faces seemed to concern our helpful server, so she went away for a few moments... only to bring back a customer who also spoke English. She happily assisted us with our order. We could have eventually ordered successfully, but the extra help was much appreciated.

At the entrance, the many attractive live fish tanks certainly caught our attention. This is a seafood lover's paradise. We ordered an array of several dishes -- some familiar, some not, but all exceptionally yummy and well prepared. They were served in a nice order about 2 at a time and we never ran out of new dishes on the table. The restaurant is so massive that kitchen servers are on roller skates to keep the food delivery hot and tasty.

Our table was surrounded by many large family gatherings who were there very much enjoying the dining occasion. This is an elegantly casual place with many beautiful sights to see while eating and enjoying your fellow guest's company.

We felt very much at home, were very well served, and had one of the most memorable food experiences ever. We had mostly moderately priced dishes and our bill was ridiculously cheap -- not much more than the round trip taxi service from our hotel (about 600,000 VND or $30 USD).

My wife and I have eaten at many Michelin star establishments all over the world, but never have we had a more tasty or delightful dinning experience. If you're adventurous and generally enjoy food from this region (especially seafood), you will fall in love with this fantastic restaurant. This was our last meal before departing Vietnam and one of our fondest memories of our month-long tour of Asia. I guarantee you won't forget the experience. Highly recommended.

Great Food Great ambiance
Nov 2015 • Family
We went twice.
First as a treat to son and daughter-in-law, second time to introduce new daughter-in-law to her extended (new) Vietnamese family.

On arrival you are taken to your dining area by a golf cart, having arrived you are met by your waitress who will relay your food / drink preferences which are likely to be delivered by a guy on roller skates - keeps the food warm.

The food is all Vietnamese - Brits can forget fish and chips and Americans will not find pizza's or tacos, all the better.

We did not hold back on the beer, wine or food for a total of 12 people the bill was around VND 3,500,000 with an exchange rate of VND 35800 +/- to GBP 1.00 that came out at around GBP97 total - inclusive, or GBp 8.00 a head!!!.
(cost me more for a burger and coke in Maidenhead, Berks, UK).

Very nice, very large place with a lot to offer.
Bit out of the way and off the tourist/backpacker route, but worth a visit, found by virtue of my Vietnamese wife's families vast knowledge of local eateries !
